scan.summary: This is an internal operating record — the daily pre-use inspection log for one propane forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse for September 2026, kept to satisfy the federal powered industrial truck examination requirement that Oregon OSHA adopts by reference. A record like this is judged on whether it is complete, current and signed off, not against a written standard: it is the evidence you would hand an inspector to show the truck was checked before use and that defects were acted on. As it stands the log has missing operating days, a recorded horn defect with no repair or return-to-service entry, entries for one shift only, no supervisor sign-off, and nothing recorded in the nine days before today.
scan.freshness_note: The last entry is 2026-09-18, nine days before today (2026-09-27). If the truck has been operated since then, the current pages of the log are missing from what was provided — ask for entries from Sep 19 through today, plus the repair record for the Sep 9 horn defect.

gaps.title: No inspection entries for Sep 3 and Sep 4 although the truck ran
gaps.description: The log jumps from Sep 2 to Sep 7. Sep 3 and Sep 4, 2026 were a Thursday and Friday, and the hour meter climbed 15 hours across the gap, so the truck was operated on days with no recorded pre-use examination.
gaps.fix: Reconstruct or, if that is not possible, note the omission and why; then tie the log to a control that prevents a truck being keyed out without a completed checklist (key/board control, or a per-truck checklist book the supervisor reconciles weekly).
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) — trucks shall be examined before being placed in service, and shall not be placed in service if the examination shows any condition adversely affecting safety; examination at least daily. Adopted in Oregon by reference at OAR 437-002-0220(3), with Oregon-specific additions at OAR 437-002-0227.
gaps.locator: page 1, log table between the 'Sep 2' and 'Sep 7' rows
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Horn defect recorded Sep 9 with no repair or return-to-service entry
gaps.description: Sep 9 shows an X in the Horn column with the note 'Horn not working'. There is no entry anywhere in the log showing the truck was taken out of service, who repaired the horn, or when it was returned to service — the Sep 10 row simply shows the horn ticked OK.
gaps.fix: Attach the work order or repair note for the horn and record the return-to-service date and who authorized it. Add a 'defect corrected / date / by whom' field to the form so the next defect closes out on the same page as it is raised.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (defects when found shall be immediately reported and corrected) and 29 CFR 1910.178(p)(1) (a truck in unsafe operating condition shall be removed from service until restored to safe operating condition)
gaps.locator: page 1, log table, 'Sep 9' row, Horn column and Notes column

gaps.title: Only day-shift checks recorded at a site your records describe as multi-shift
gaps.description: Every row in the log is marked 'Day'. Your own site facts record that the Portland site operates multiple shifts. If FL-2 is used on a later shift, that shift's examination is neither performed nor recorded.
gaps.fix: Either add a row per shift the truck is used, or record in writing that FL-2 is a day-shift-only asset and is locked out at end of day shift.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) — where industrial trucks are used on a round-the-clock basis, they shall be examined after each shift
gaps.quote: Date Shift Hours Tires Forks Mast Horn Lights Belt Brakes Steering LPG Ext. Plate Guard Operator Notes

gaps.title: No entries after Sep 18 — the record is nine days stale
gaps.description: The last row is Sep 18, 2026. There are no entries for Sep 21, 22, 23, 24 or 25 (weekdays) or since. Either the truck sat idle and nobody noted it, or checks were done and not written down, or checks were not done.
gaps.fix: Produce the missing pages if they exist; if the truck was out of use, write a one-line note on the log saying so with dates.

gaps.title: Supervisor review line left blank
gaps.description: The form provides for a supervisor review signature and date at the end of the month; both are empty. Nobody has signed to say the month's entries — including the Sep 9 defect — were looked at.
gaps.fix: Have the warehouse supervisor review and sign the September sheet, and set a fixed day each month for the review.
gaps.citation: No federal or Oregon rule requires the supervisor signature — it is a control this form sets for itself, so the blank is an unmet internal step rather than a rule breach. I am confident there is no signature requirement in 1910.178(q)(7).
